newsitem.title: CHINA: China motor vehicle insurance up 25 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China motor vehicle insurance up 25 pct in 1996.

text.p: China's total premium earnings from motor vehicle insurance reached 26 billion yuan last year, up 25 percent from 1995, statistics from the Pacific Ocean Insurance Co showed on Tuesday.

The figure accounted for nearly 60 percent of total domestic premium earnings from property insurance, the Xinhua news agency quoted Xu Jinghui, deputy manager of the Domestic Business Department of Pacific Ocean Insurance Co, as saying.
Motor insurance has become the most important source of income and profit for Chinese property insurance companies and would see rapid growth in coming years, Xu told a seminar in Beijing.
By 2000, China will have 16 million motor vehicles for civilian use and 1.2 million km of roads, Xu said, but gave no comparative figures.
Based on this, China's premiums from motor vehicle insurance were expected to top 45 billion yuan by the end of the century, growing at an average annual rate of about 20 percent, he said.
The giant People's Insurance Company of China (PICC) still held 80.7 percent of the domestic motor vehicle insurance market, he said.
Claims were also rising, with China's big three insurers, PICC, Pacific Ocean Insurance and Ping'an Insurance, paying a total of 15 billion yuan in claims last year, he said.
